_doc: What exists in the multilingual worker layer. See docs/WORKERS.md. A missing artifact is reported as [skip], never as a pass.

_schema.build: argv, run from the repository root, once per run when the artifact is missing or older than the sources
_schema.artifact: path that must exist after a successful build

workers.notes: the reference implementation, and a worker like the others: it is diffed against them rather than trusted. No build step.
the reference implementation of search.query (docs/WORKERS.md section 9): integers only, a total ordering, and the same tokenizer as text.fingerprint. No build step.

the reference implementation of llm.parse (docs/WORKERS.md section 11): the believing half of the LLM glue. Asking a model is I/O and stays in the application; parsing, repairing and checking the answer is pure text work, and that is the part several languages get subtly different. No build step.
the reference implementation of fetch.plan (docs/WORKERS.md section 10): pure planning, no clock of its own, integers only. No build step.
JDK 17, no third-party libraries, table-driven normalizer
C++17, no third-party libraries, tables embedded at build time
Go, standard library only: the fetch.plan planner, exact integer arithmetic, no clock of its own
Python 3.13, standard library only, no build step (build.mjs only checks the interpreter)
Python 3.13, standard library only, no build step: ASCII-only whitespace and folding, a strict RFC 8259 parse, and truncation by code points

PowerShell 7, no modules, no compilation (the artifact IS the script); build.mjs only checks the interpreter, the shared tables and the built-in self-check. -NoProfile keeps a user profile out of the protocol stream, -NonInteractive keeps a prompt from becoming a stdout line.
JDK 17, no dependencies, an inverted index (token -> posting list with per-field presence), integers only
search.query expressed in SQLite through node:sqlite: the filters, the integer score, the ordering and the facets are SQL; no build step, no third-party packages

.NET 8+, BCL only, no packages: the shared tables are read from workers/spec at startup, and every comparison is ordinal or explicitly invariant because .NET's case and trim defaults are culture-aware

_planned: No new languages for now: this layer is consolidating. The published set is JavaScript, Java, C++, Go, Python, PowerShell and SQL, and every capability has at least two implementations - six for the text capabilities, three for search.query, two each for fetch.plan and llm.parse.

The machine-local workers (r-text, bash-text, j-text) live in workers/registry.local.json, which is gitignored, because their interpreters are not on every machine and the published registry must never depend on one. Their sources are tracked; only the launch command is local.

A language whose interpreter cannot read a live pipe is not excluded: give its registry entry "batch": true and the harness writes every case and then closes stdin (docs/WORKERS.md section 1.3). That is how the J worker is registered, and it is the durable result of the attempt - the worker itself is a documented experiment rather than an implementation this layer counts on.
upc / linux: see the portability section of docs/WORKERS.md
